questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I would like to go to Norway, because i like nature and doing outdoor activities. The reason i went to Oslo was for the course Fungal Biology at UiO, which they didn't have in CPH or anywhere else in Norway.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Kind of easy. There was a lot of work beforehand, but i was always able to email UCPH abroad for help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received e-mails from the university of Oslo, and "their exchange student help desk" was very helpful with answering any questions i had.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was helped through SIO which made it so easy to be a student in Oslo, they have everything you need and also housing opportunities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You have to get yourself traintickets to get to campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy and resembled the danish system a lot. You applied for the courses you wanted at studentweb, and then you could see when the deadline for application was and when it would close. You could apply for more courses than you needed, and even when arriving in Oslo they gave us information on the application for courses which was still open at that time. This made it a lot easier.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could write an e-mail and you would get a reply back really fast, but the course registration was not closed upon arrival and they held an introduction lecture to the university and the course registration and everything.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100% succesful. I didn't get 2 out of 3 of the courses i wanted the most, but since i was put on waiting list i got in after the start of the semester, where a lot of people cancel their registrations to the courses. This meant i got all 3 of the courses i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To have patience. Sign up for more courses than the ones you really want, show up to all the first lectures and then give it a week or two, and then you might get a spot on the course even though it was originally full.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The teachers were amazing. Some of the best teaching i ever had.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: You don't have a lot of physical attendance compared to the university in Copenhagen. I would say that the level is a little lower, but i don't necesarrily see this as a bad thing. I learned a lot, and when the study burden is a little lower, you are able to take more in, in my opinion.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In the biology courses there was possibility to go on field trips, the style of teaching was very immersive and required that the students took active part in the teaching. I would say the teachers were very dedicated and skilled, and i really enjoyed the courses. But maybe i was just really lucky with my courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Fungal Biology
Applied ethics
Framing the environment in social media and communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All three of them.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I broke my ankle and had surgery - but if you are from Scandinavia you are able to go to the hospital for free in Norway (very very nice), but there was some additional fees for x-ray and doctors appointments outside the hospital that my insurance didn't cover.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and beer was very expensive in Norway.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Everything you could dream of, they had an association for everything. I didn't attend any, but the possibility was there.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: They offer a river-paddling course, this looked dope but i couldn't go because it was filled

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go skiing in the winter at tryvann, go skating (Oslo have a great skate scene, also for women), visit Sognsvann, go hiking in any of the nearby fjelds, go to Bergen, go climbing or bouldering (also great oppurtinites in oslo)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, im from denmark and i went to norway, it's almost the same

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Try to learn a bit of norwegian beforehand

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier at times. Some norwegians had a hard time understanding danish, and it was sometimes hard to understand norwegian, and it is not very cool to speak english when your languages are so similar hehe

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outdoor-appreciation-culture and the availability of extreme sports

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: To enjoy it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: no

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To meet a lot of norwegian people that i can visit and experience the beautiful nature in Norway.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To understand and be understood

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
